title: Chapter 43 — The Renovation Contractor
intro: The highest-frequency account in residential trade — the chaos they live in and the behaviours that make you infrastructure.

sections.title: The Renovation Reality
sections.content:
Renovation contractors live in chaos. Their schedules change daily. Clients change their minds. Subcontractors no-show. Materials are backordered. And in the middle of all of it, they need appliances to show up at the right time in the right condition.

They do not have time for slow quotes, complicated processes, or salespeople who need to 'check and get back to them.' They need speed, accuracy, and reliability.

sections.title: What Makes You Infrastructure
sections.content:
Respond to quote requests the same day — ideally within hours. Know their typical price range and have packages ready. Understand construction timelines — do not deliver appliances to a job site where the drywall is not up yet. Be flexible on delivery windows because their schedule shifts constantly.

When they text you at 7 AM asking if you can add a hood to tomorrow's delivery, say yes. That kind of responsiveness is what turns a vendor into infrastructure. Once you are infrastructure, they stop shopping around.

sections.title: The Split Account Warning
sections.content:
A renovation contractor who uses you for half their projects and a competitor for the other half is a split account. A split account is best read as a warning — not a win. It means you have not earned enough trust to consolidate their business.

Find out why they split. Is it price? Product availability? Delivery flexibility? A relationship with the other rep? Then address the specific gap. The goal is 100 percent of their flow, not 50 percent.
